close_reason: Done in 8a18b8b. Added 'Do not simplify the wrappers' module-docstring section to error.rs enumerating the five reasons HttpError/WebSocketError/InvalidHeaderValueError exist. Pins the rationale at the call site of any future 'just expose reqwest::Error' refactor proposal.
description:
error.rs:34, 112, 178 define three opaque wrapper types around reqwest::Error, tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::Error, and reqwest::header::InvalidHeaderValue. Each wrapper exposes a hand-curated set of accessor methods (is_timeout, is_connect, status, url for HttpError; is_io, is_protocol, etc for WebSocketError) that return primitive types only.

A contributor may suggest 'just put reqwest::Error in the variant, downstream users want the full reqwest API'. This is the wrong simplification.

Defense:
1. reqwest::Error and tungstenite::Error are #[non_exhaustive] from third-party crates that bump major versions independently of this crate. Exposing them in this crate's public API means every reqwest major bump is a SemVer break for every downstream extension client.
2. This crate's AGENTS.md lines 28-32 explicitly documents this as intentional after bd:JMAP-6lsm.22.
3. The wrapper-types pattern lets this crate swap the HTTP/WebSocket transport entirely (e.g. ureq, hyper directly) without breaking downstream — the only thing downstream binds to is the wrapper's accessor signature.
4. error.rs:382-401 construction goes through pub(crate) helpers (from_reqwest, from_ws, from_invalid_header) so downstream cannot construct the transport-error variants. This makes the wrappers genuinely opaque.
5. The accessor set is curated — not every reqwest::Error method is mirrored — which forces a deliberate decision when adding new diagnostic surface.

This is a deliberate boundary, not an oversight. Resist requests to 'just unwrap the reqwest::Error'.
title: SemVer-isolation via HttpError/WebSocketError/InvalidHeaderValueError wrappers: defend against 'just expose reqwest::Error'
